bull_bear.body: Net cash positive balance sheet maintained. Gross debt capped at 0.75x D/E. Strategy to recover commercial development costs via partial sales (60-65%) to funds/HNIs while retaining income-generating assets. No dividend mentioned; focus on reinvestment for INR10k cr target.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Execution risk on large cluster redevelopments; Interest rate sensitivity affecting affordable/mid-segment demand (INR1-3 cr); Commodity price volatility (steel, cement); Regulatory delays in redevelopment approvals; Collection efficiency dilution due to high proportion of new launches.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Highly confident, disciplined, and forward-looking. Emphasizes 'inflection point,' 'keeping commitments,' and 'structural multi-decade demand cycle.' Transparent on accounting changes and legacy exit.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Shift to POCM accounting will make financials mirror operational strength immediately rather than upon completion. Precast technology adoption is a defensive moat against future labor shortages and a margin lever. Commercial strategy pivots from pure strata sale to 'develop-sell-retain' annuity model to de-lever balance sheet.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Balance sheet as on 30-Jun-26: gross debt INR 8,759 Mn, cash and equivalents INR 8,032 Mn, net debt INR 728 Mn against equity of INR 29,248 Mn; Gross D/E 0.30 and Net D/E 0.02 (versus 0.26 and nil at 31-Mar-26). Debt in JV Co. (KRL share) INR 908 Mn.
- Asset-light acquisition rule: "Acquire projects having GDV of 2x of the previous year pre-sales through Asset-Light model i.e JDA/JV", with tenders described as an emerging key supply enabler in land-scarce Mumbai.
- Credit profile: dual "AA- / Stable" from CRISIL Ratings and ICRA, following a ladder of ICRA A- (Feb 2024), ICRA A (May 2024), ICRA A+ (May 2025), CRISIL AA- (May 2026) and ICRA AA- (June 2026).
- Third-party capital is structural: Mt. K Kapital (SEBI Category II AIF, anchored by State Bank of India and Famy Group) invests in several projects; strategic/PE partners over time include HDFC Capital, IIFL Special Opportunities Funds, Xander-advised entities and Keppel Land (via Lipalton Pte. Ltd. in Kapstone).
- Funding milestones on the journey slide: QIP raised in 2024 and a maiden listed NCD issued successfully in 2026; the deck states INR 48 Bn of sold receivables locked-in.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Three decades of delivery in a single region: over 29 million square feet of construction area developed, more than 320 buildings completed, more than 19,000 homes delivered and more than 1,900 families rehoused
- Redevelopment franchise built on the trust of housing societies - of the 25 projects added since FY23, 21 are redevelopment, and redevelopment accounts for approximately 74% of the forthcoming portfolio in GDV terms
- Deliberate concentration in the Mumbai Metropolitan Region, where roughly 70% of the city's land is already built upon, giving detailed knowledge of micro-markets, societies and buyers
- Asset-light model: equity limited to approximately 10% of project value on new additions, with new projects underwritten at approximately 35% blended gross margin before they are added
- Integrated in-house platform across business development, architecture and design, approvals, construction management, sales and marketing, and post-handover property management
- Premium-skewed portfolio - approximately 94% of the forthcoming residential portfolio is emerging premium or premium, and approximately 92% of FY26 residential pre-sales came from premium categories
- Net cash balance sheet through FY26 with a credit rating upgraded to CRISIL AA- with a stable outlook
- Cluster redevelopment capability - five clusters with combined estimated GDV of approximately Rs 13,700 crore, a format that spreads fixed costs and lifts blended margins
- Move to advanced precast and pre-fitted construction, reducing dependence on a shrinking pool of skilled site labour
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Input cost inflation — Management lists inflation first among its principal risks: escalating input costs may adversely affect profitability and the financial viability of projects - material for a developer whose reported FY26 margins already reflect the completion of older, lower-margin projects.
- Project execution delays — Delays in project execution and delivery may increase construction and maintenance expenses, compressing margins and damaging customer satisfaction; in a pre-sales-and-collections model, delivery timing also drives revenue recognition and cash flow.
- Regulatory change — Amendments to government policies or regulatory frameworks may affect business operations and compliance requirements - acute for a business dependent on redevelopment approvals and long approval cycles.
- Shifts in consumer preference — Evolving market trends and customer expectations can influence sales performance and project outcomes; the portfolio has been deliberately skewed towards premium and emerging premium, so a change in buyer preference bears directly on absorption.
- Brand reputation — Any lapse in maintaining the Company's brand reputation could diminish market position and erode customer loyalty; the redevelopment model depends on the trust of housing societies, and suboptimal customer experiences are separately flagged as a source of reputational harm and lost future business.
- Talent management — The ability to attract, develop and retain skilled professionals is described as critical to sustaining operational efficiency and organisational growth; employee engagement and welfare programmes are the stated mitigation.
- Fraud and unethical practices — Incidents of fraud or unethical conduct could compromise the Company's reputation and financial stability; mitigated through enforced corporate governance policies, a structured risk system with named ownership, a Chief Risk Officer and internal audit reporting directly to the Audit Committee.
- Water scarcity at project sites — Identified in the BRSR material-issues table as a risk with negative financial implications - water is an important construction resource and scarcity may disrupt operations and delay project completion timelines; mitigated through conservation strategies, rainwater harvesting at some facilities, external procurement and an EHS policy tied to ISO 14001:2015 objectives.
- Climate change and extreme weather — Identified in the BRSR material-issues table as a risk with negative financial implications - cyclones, fires, droughts and heat waves can severely disrupt operations and expose workers; mitigation covers Scope 1 and 2 emission controls, hazard identification and emergency response plans, and supplier engagement on ESG compliance.

business.body: Residential (Emerging Premium INR1-3 cr, Premium INR3-7 cr, Super Premium INR7-15 cr) constitutes 94% of forthcoming pipeline. business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- Three-pillar snapshot: "MMR FOCUSED", "PROMINENT REDEVELOPMENT BRAND" and "ASSET LIGHT MODEL", backed by 30+ years of existence, 29+ msf construction area developed, 46 msf construction area in pipeline, 2 mega townships, 320+ completed buildings and 19,000+ homes delivered (incl 1900+ rehoused).
- Redevelopment dominance: "76% Forthcoming projects (In GDV terms) are redevelopment (excluding township)"; the deck calls the company a "PIONEER IN LARGE SCALE SOCIETY REDEVELOPMENT" with 1900+ homes rehoused and proven expertise in societies with over 400 members.
- Opportunity framing (source: Knight Frank 2025): 70% of open land in Mumbai is already developed, >1.6 lakh societies are 30+ years old, 70% to 85% of new supply in matured micro markets comes from redevelopment, and housing society redevelopment alone in Mumbai is stated as an INR 1,300 Bn opportunity by 2030.
- Redevelopment economics claimed as structurally superior: "Lower upfront land cost -> lower capital employed -> improved IRRs", with strategic locations secured at minimal land acquisition investment in Western and Central suburbs described as Rustomjee's core strongholds.
- End-to-end in-house capability across Business Development, Architecture/design, Approvals, Construction Management, Sales & Marketing and Property Management Services.

business.body:
- [Shareholding] As on 30 June 2026: Promoter 74.59%, Mutual Funds 8.37%, Insurance 5.51%, Others 5.35%, AIF 2.50%, FPI 2.36%, Bodies Corporate 1.32%.
- [JV economics] Stated economic interests differ from headline project scale: Urbania 51%, Charkop 73%, Manori 73%, Goregaon JV 51%, Haren Textiles 51%, 33Fifteen ~50%, Bandstand ~33%; 180 Bayview (Jariwala) is a DM project with a fee of 17% of project revenue plus incentive fee.
- [Ecosystem] Three adjacent platforms: Mt. K Kapital (Category II AIF, first fund is an ESG impact fund focused on MMR residential), CREST property management services, and Fifth Wall Designs (interiors for residential clients).
- [Technology] Migrated core ERP from SAP ECC to RISE with SAP, runs Autodesk Construction Cloud and Salesforce CRM, completed Phase 1 of enterprise server consolidation, and launched an "AI Next" adoption initiative training 100+ employees.
- [Guidance gap] The deck itself shows FY27 YTD pre-sales of INR 6.2 Bn against INR 50 Bn full-year guidance and NIL launches against INR 80 Bn guidance, attributed to a "no-launch quarter" carried by sustenance sales.
business.title: Notable from the deck

business.body: Keystone Realtors Limited develops residential real estate across the full spectrum of the Mumbai Metropolitan Region market - premium gated communities, integrated townships and high-rise towers - complemented by a growing commercial and plotted development portfolio. Its distinguishing business is the redevelopment of ageing housing societies in dense urban micro-markets, where it partners with societies and landowners rather than buying land outright, and it classifies its residential projects into five ticket-size categories from mass market to luxury. The Company runs the entire development value chain in-house, from business development, architecture and approvals through construction management, sales and marketing to post-handover property management under the CREST platform.

outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Scale the redevelopment franchise in the Mumbai Metropolitan Region, a business the Company has participated in for over 25 years and which depends on the trust of the families whose homes it redevelops
- Increase focus on cluster redevelopment - bringing multiple adjoining buildings and societies into one development for better planning, larger open spaces and greater scale per mandate - with positions strengthened during the year at GTB Nagar (Sion), Lokhandwala (Andheri W), Dindoshi (Goregaon E), Om Nagar (Andheri E) and Malad West
- Grow presence in the premium and emerging premium segments, where the forthcoming portfolio is concentrated
- Enter new micro-markets selectively, studying infrastructure development, population movement and demand before committing
- Add velocity through new geographies and new formats such as plotted development, and through faster project activation
- Build a commercial portfolio - marked by the launch of 33Fifteen in Bandra West - to complement the residential platform and create a long-term annuity stream
- Maintain the asset-light model, limiting upfront equity in new projects to approximately 10% of project GDV, with every opportunity evaluated for location, demand, margins and capital efficiency
- Preserve a net cash balance sheet and disciplined capital allocation, reflected in the dual AA- (Stable) ratings from ICRA and CRISIL
- Adopt advanced precast construction technology, with technical, engineering and supervision support from Robin Village Development of Singapore, to improve quality and precision, accelerate execution, cut material wastage and offset pressure on skilled manpower
- Progressively apply Artificial Intelligence across planning, design, customer engagement, sales and operations
- Pursue sustainability goals of a fully green-certified portfolio by 2030 and carbon neutrality by 2050, with continued focus on safety and worker welfare
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Expansion for Keystone Realtors is project-pipeline expansion rather than plant capex. Six developments comprising 2.23 million square feet of construction area were completed during FY26 - Paramount Wing F (Khar W), Crown Tower Wing C (Prabhadevi), Belle Vue Phase 1 (Kasara), Cleon (Bandra E), Bella Wings A and B (Bhandup) and Virar Retail (Virar) - taking the cumulative body of work past 320 buildings, 19,000 homes and 29 million square feet of construction area. Seventeen projects are under way with a combined gross development value of Rs 19,242 crore and 8.69 million square feet of saleable area, approximately 49% already sold; these span the Global City (Virar W) and Urbania (Thane W) townships, fifteen residential and commercial projects including Ashiana, Aden, Stella, Panorama, 180 Bayview, Ocean Vista, Urban Woods Phase 1, Prive, Balmoral Golf Links, Cliff Tower, Crescent Apartments, Bandstand Cama, Vista Bay and the 33Fifteen commercial project, plus Belle Vue Phase 2 at Kasara as a plotted development. The forthcoming pipeline is 21 projects with combined GDV of Rs 42,698 crore and 21.44 million square feet of saleable area, roughly 94% of the forthcoming residential portfolio in the emerging premium and premium segments, and includes five cluster redevelopments (GTB Nagar at Sion, Lokhandwala at Andheri W, Dindoshi at Goregaon E, Om Nagar at Andheri E and Malad W), two integrated townships, commercial developments at Thane, OB12 + 13 (Bandra E) and Dhuru Wadi (Prabhadevi), and the Manori plotted development, together with residential schemes at Charkop, Ozone Phase II, Dombivli, Ambedkar Nagar, Haren Textiles, Goregaon JV, Avinash Towers, Shivneri, Pardi (Nagpur) and Enticer (Thane). Several are held at partial economic interest - Urbania 51%, Charkop 73%, Manori 73%, Goregaon JV 51%, Haren Textiles 51%, 33Fifteen 50%, Bandstand 33% - and at Virar 2.8 million square feet of forthcoming saleable area is to be developed under a joint development agreement (1.4 million square feet was launched under a JDA with multiple developers in the ongoing portfolio). Redevelopment underpins the growth: of the 25 projects added since FY23, 21 are redevelopment, accounting for approximately 74% of the forthcoming portfolio in GDV terms, and it is pursued with minimal land acquisition investment, lower capital employed and improved project IRRs. Structurally, the Company incorporated eight new subsidiaries and JVs during FY26 (Keymidtown Developers, Keyvian Realtors, Keyastren Realtors, Keynivara Realtors, Keyorion Realtors, Keyamoura Realtors, Keylinzia Realtors and Key Stone Ventures LLP), ending the year with 62 subsidiaries including 3 LLPs, 3 associates and 6 joint ventures.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Indian residential demand held broadly steady in 2025 while new launches moderated, keeping supply disciplined relative to absorption and preventing inventory accumulation
- The premiumisation trend appears structural, with buyers and developers gravitating to mid-premium and luxury housing; homes priced above Rs 10 million have become the dominant force in the market
- Infrastructure-led growth opens new geographies and micro-markets - the FY26 Budget allocated Rs 11.21 lakh crore to capital expenditure, and metro, airport and freight-corridor programmes are expanding satellite towns and peripheral suburbs
- The developer universe continues to institutionalise and consolidate, with organised, trusted developers extending market share
- An improving financing environment - inflation at multi-year lows and the policy repo rate eased to 5.25% - should lower mortgage costs and improve credit availability, supporting demand at the affordability margin
- Knight Frank estimates approximately 78 million new homes will be needed between 2024 and 2034 as the young population urbanises, with the sector contributing approximately 10.5% of GDP by 2034
- MMR remained resilient: 2025 residential sales of approximately 97,188 units (up 1%), launches down about 10% to approximately 87,114 units, weighted average price up approximately 7% to around Rs 95,326 per square metre
- MMR unsold inventory fell about 6% to approximately 155,604 units with a quarters-to-sell ratio of 6.4, pointing to genuine end-user demand and price stability
- Redevelopment is the primary source of new supply in mature Mumbai micro-markets, accounting for an estimated 70% to 85% of new supply, with the housing society redevelopment opportunity placed at approximately Rs 1,30,000 crore by 2030
- Emerging premium and premium segments account for approximately 94% of the Company's forthcoming residential portfolio, aligning the pipeline with where demand is shifting
- Demand for quality homes entering FY27 is supported by favourable demographics, infrastructure-led growth, urban renewal and rising aspirations for home ownership
- FY26 pre-sales of Rs 4,022 crore, the Company's highest ever, up 33% year-on-year, with collections of Rs 2,621 crore (up 13%) and operating cash flow of Rs 715 crore
- Pre-sales have grown from Rs 1,604 crore in FY23 to Rs 4,022 crore in FY26, a compound annual growth rate of approximately 36%, while MMR market share has approximately doubled
- Seven projects launched during FY26 with an estimated GDV of Rs 9,813 crore
- Five new projects added to the future pipeline during FY26 with an estimated GDV of Rs 10,420 crore, weighted to larger redevelopment opportunities and the premium segments
- Large cluster opportunities strengthened during the year at GTB Nagar (Sion), Lokhandwala (Andheri W), Dindoshi (Goregaon E), Om Nagar (Andheri E) and Malad West

risks.note: Management lists inflation first among its principal risks: escalating input costs may adversely affect profitability and the financial viability of projects - material for a developer whose reported FY26 margins already reflect the completion of older, lower-margin projects.

Delays in project execution and delivery may increase construction and maintenance expenses, compressing margins and damaging customer satisfaction; in a pre-sales-and-collections model, delivery timing also drives revenue recognition and cash flow.

Amendments to government policies or regulatory frameworks may affect business operations and compliance requirements - acute for a business dependent on redevelopment approvals and long approval cycles.

Evolving market trends and customer expectations can influence sales performance and project outcomes; the portfolio has been deliberately skewed towards premium and emerging premium, so a change in buyer preference bears directly on absorption.

Any lapse in maintaining the Company's brand reputation could diminish market position and erode customer loyalty; the redevelopment model depends on the trust of housing societies, and suboptimal customer experiences are separately flagged as a source of reputational harm and lost future business.

The ability to attract, develop and retain skilled professionals is described as critical to sustaining operational efficiency and organisational growth; employee engagement and welfare programmes are the stated mitigation.

Incidents of fraud or unethical conduct could compromise the Company's reputation and financial stability; mitigated through enforced corporate governance policies, a structured risk system with named ownership, a Chief Risk Officer and internal audit reporting directly to the Audit Committee.

Identified in the BRSR material-issues table as a risk with negative financial implications - water is an important construction resource and scarcity may disrupt operations and delay project completion timelines; mitigated through conservation strategies, rainwater harvesting at some facilities, external procurement and an EHS policy tied to ISO 14001:2015 objectives.
